pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: features/dukazy/DukazyPage.tsx:84 /dukazy prints each review_audit row's chain position and row_hash, and its chain.note copy tells readers the hash proves order and non-tampering. But nothing on the read path (readReviewAudit → getDukazyData → page and feedCodecs) recomputes the chain: verifyAuditChain/verifyReviewChain are called only from tests and lib/testing/sentinel. A tampered row would therefore be published with the same confident hash and no verified/tampered verdict.

techniques.evidence: features/dukazy/DukazyPage.tsx:84 The technique says to verify on read and give a verdict with four values. This surface shows the stored hash and never recomputes it, so by the technique's own words the proof is decoration.

features/dukazy/readReviewAudit.ts:68 A capped read is detected and passed to the surface as a floor rather than a count. Line 65 returns null for an unreadable store, which is kept separate from an empty journal ({rows: []}).
features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:281 The identity of a human decision is built from durable endpoints (src/rel/dst) and the audit-row uuid, not from wording. Line 275 carries priorState next to the act.
features/dukazy/getDukazyData.ts:2 This context only consumes the ledger and exposes no write or mutation surface. The ledger's module shape lives in lib/db.
features/dukazy/deriveFeed.ts:15 Nothing is written here, so write-path scrubbing does not apply. The publication side does withhold the reviewer's free-text note on purpose.

pairs.subject: audit-logging
pairs.evidence: features/votetrack/ledgerRead.ts:1 VoteTrack is a read path over the external PSP10 vote record (vote_event/vote_ballot), not a ledger of actions this system took. A case-insensitive grep of features/votetrack for audit, tamper, row_hash, chain_pos, review_audit and reviewer returned no hits, so the subject's precondition does not hold.
